title: Where Your Spotify Money Actually Goes
description:
Where Your Spotify Money Actually Goes.

Sources:

hook.prompt: Cinematic photo, vertical: a pair of wireless earbuds in an open case on a dark surface, glowing ribbons of colorful light flowing out like sound waves, moody, photorealistic, no text, no logos

mid.prompt: Cinematic photo, vertical: a wall of framed gold and platinum records in a dark music label office, one spotlight, vinyl records on a shelf below, rich gold tones, photorealistic, no readable text, no logos, no artist names

scenes.narration: Spotify brought in billions last year. Most of it wasn't Spotify's to keep.
In 2025, Spotify paid more than 11 billion dollars to the music industry, the biggest yearly payout of any music service ever.

visual.label: paid to the music industry in 2025

scenes.narration: That's roughly 70 cents of every music dollar going to labels, publishers and distributors.

visual.label: of music revenue goes to rights holders

scenes.narration: And it goes to rights holders, not straight to artists. Their record deals decide how much artists actually see.
Spotify keeps about 30 cents, and uses it to build podcasts, audiobooks and video. Follow for more.
